title: Reservations, Courtesy Holds and Ticket Issue on Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand
content:
**Reservations desk manual — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** A reservation is created in the held state for one passenger on one fare brand, and the fare brand's booking conditions (cabin, corporate or award booking, itinerary classes sold) must hold at booking.

## 1. Courtesy hold

1.1 When the fare brand's courtesy hold is zero hours, the reservation must be paid and ticketed in the same transaction.

1.2 A held reservation can be ticketed only while its courtesy hold is open, that is no later than the moment the reservation is placed on courtesy hold plus the fare brand's courtesy hold hours.

1.3 The hold window is counted in full elapsed hours from the booking timestamp recorded on the reservation, and a ticketing attempt at exactly the end of the window is still inside it. The clock is the system record of the booking moment; a customer's recollection of when the booking was made does not replace it.

1.4 A hold that passes the end of its window unpaid lapses and its seats are released. A lapsed reservation is never reinstated, and the customer books again at the fare then available.

| Situation (24-hour courtesy hold, booked at 09:00 on day 1 — hypothetical) | Ticketing |
|---|---|
| Ticketing at 08:59 on day 2 | Inside the window |
| Ticketing at exactly 09:00 on day 2 | Inside the window (end of window counts) |
| Ticketing at 09:01 on day 2 | Past the window; the hold has lapsed |

## 2. Ticket issue and ticket value

2.1 Ticketing collects the full fare, the base fare plus taxes and fees, in one fare-collection entry in the form of payment recorded on the ticket, and the ticket's residual value opens at that amount.

2.2 A ticket paid with a flight credit draws that value from the credit; a ticket paid with award miles has its miles taken by the Summit award redemption; a companion ticket draws one companion trip from the companion certificate or pass.

2.3 The residual value always equals every fare-collection and add-collect entry less every coupon, conversion, refund, residual and forfeiture entry on the ticket.

*Hypothetical example.* A base fare of 312.00 dollars with taxes and fees of 41.20 dollars is collected as one entry of 353.20 dollars, and the residual value opens at 353.20 dollars.

## 3. Ticket validity

3.1 Travel on the ticket must begin within the fare brand's ticket validity period in calendar months of issue, counted from the issue date to the same day-of-month, falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist.

| Issue date (hypothetical) | Validity of 12 months ends |
|---|---|
| 10 March 2027 | 10 March 2028 |
| 29 February 2028 | 28 February 2029 (the 29th does not exist) |
